name: DMR
description: Digital Mobile Radio, the ETSI standard (TS 102 361) for digital voice and data radio, used on amateur repeaters and linked networks.
howItWorks: Two-slot TDMA on a 12.5 kHz carrier: two independent channels (timeslots 1 and 2) share one frequency. 4FSK modulation at 4,800 symbols/s, 2 bits per symbol. A 4-bit colour code (CC 0–15) tells overlapping sites apart.
useCases: Voice and data through repeaters, organised by timeslot and talkgroup; wide-area linking between repeaters.
equipmentNeeded: A DMR radio programmed with the repeater's frequencies, colour code, timeslot and talkgroup.

name: D-STAR
description: The digital voice and data system specified by JARL, the Japan Amateur Radio League.
howItWorks: Voice: AMBE codec at 2.4 kbps (3.6 kbps with error correction) in a stream of up to 4.8 kbps, occupying up to 6 kHz, on channels at least 6.25 kHz apart; GMSK modulation. Data: up to 128 kbps in up to 150 kHz, simplex.
useCases: Digital voice through repeaters with data alongside; high-speed data; repeater-to-repeater links on 5.6 GHz and higher bands.

name: C4FM / System Fusion
description: Yaesu's C4FM digital voice and data system, known as System Fusion.
howItWorks: C4FM digital modulation. System Fusion repeaters such as Yaesu's DR-2X handle both C4FM digital and analog FM on the same repeater.
useCases: Digital voice on System Fusion repeaters; internet linking through Yaesu WIRES-X.

name: APRS
description: Automatic Packet Reporting System. In the words of its creator, WB4APR, a two-way tactical real-time digital communications system for sharing information about the local area — not a vehicle tracking system.
howItWorks: Stations send AX.25 UI frames that generic digipeaters repeat, and the APRS-IS internet backbone links worldwide. The IARU Region 1 band plans use 144.800 MHz, and 432.500 MHz on 70 cm.
useCases: Positions, objects, weather reports, messages and bulletins shared with everyone in the area.
equipmentNeeded: A radio with a built-in APRS modem, or a radio with a TNC or software modem.

name: FT8
description: A weak-signal digital mode in the WSJT-X software.
howItWorks: 8-GFSK at 6.25 baud in a 50 Hz-wide signal. Each 12.6 s transmission carries a 77-bit message protected by an LDPC (174,91) code, sent in time-synchronised transmit and receive periods.
useCases: Short, structured contacts under very weak conditions: WSJT-X quotes a decode threshold of about −21 dB S/N.
equipmentNeeded: An SSB transceiver connected to a computer running WSJT-X.

name: JS8Call
description: Keyboard-to-keyboard HF messaging using the weak-signal JS8 protocol, built on the WSJT-X / FT8 engine. Now maintained as JS8Call-Improved.
howItWorks: JS8 transmissions, decodable down to about −24 dB SNR, carry real-time chat, directed and relayed messages (including store-and-forward), heartbeats and automatic acknowledgements.
useCases: Emergency and grid-down communications, preparedness and regional nets, and everyday HF messaging.
equipmentNeeded: An HF transceiver connected to a computer running JS8Call.
